scope: codec -58 is VARIABLE-LENGTH: an all-zero value costs 39 payload bits, a large value costs 45

derivation.conclusion: the -58 payload length depends on the VALUE, so it is a variable-length (magnitude-coded) float, not a fixed 32/45-bit field

reading: this explains why an all-zero ps block was cheap (28 bits in the earliest experiments) while any large value blew the budget
it also means padding cannot fix the block: the length is a function of the value, and the decoder always reads exactly what the value implies
the block still terminates cleanly (error 0) and the actors entry is reached, so the framing is right - only the value coding model was wrong
next: measure the length function: encode several magnitudes (0, 1, 0x100, 0x10000, 0x1000000, 0x3F800000) in one session and record the ps length for each
that yields the bit-length table for -58, which is the last missing piece for writing a coherent playerstate origin
